Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Rae: Hey, could you drop your full budget workbook in the family drive by Sunday? We're trying to figure out summer cabin costs and the move-in overlap.
Mina: I can help with the planning, but I'd rather not share my full records or bank and card statements. There's personal stuff in there, and some of it isn't relevant.
Dev: Totally fair. Rae, do you mostly need Mina's monthly totals, or are you asking for every transaction so you can estimate what everyone can chip in?
Rae: Mostly the monthly totals, but I thought the detail might make it easier. The cabin deposit is due April 18, and the van needs booking soon.
Mina: I can send a category summary instead, with the amounts rounded and no account numbers or individual purchases. That should give you a useful picture without sharing the whole file. 🙂
Rae: That works. I wasn't trying to pry; I just didn't want us to miss a bill while we price the trip and the new place.
Mina: I know, and thanks for asking first. My take-home pay was about $4,180 last month; it changes a little when I pick up a weekend shift.
Mina: For March, rent was $1,460, utilities came to $185, and groceries were around $510. The utility total includes heat, power, and the building's water charge.
Dev: Are those grocery numbers just your share, or do they include the stuff you buy for your dad when you visit on Thursdays?
Mina: Mostly my share. There's usually another $35 or $40 for Dad's pantry items, and I don't track those in the same category every month.
Mina: Transit was $96, phone was $54, and the student loan payment was $230. The loan comes out on the 12th, and my phone bill is due on the 21st.
Rae: Helpful, thanks. Did you include the $400 transfer to savings in that monthly list, or do you count that separately from bills?
Mina: Separately. I move $400 after payday when I can, but that's a goal, not a fixed bill. If the car needs work, I transfer less.
Dev: We should probably keep trip costs separate from household budgets anyway. My spreadsheet has the cabin, gas, and food estimates, not anyone's personal spending.
Rae: Yes, that makes sense. I was thinking a shared budget could tell us what feels comfortable, but nobody needs to upload statements to do that.
Mina: Exactly. I'll put together a one-page summary with take-home range, fixed bills, and a rough flexible-spending total. I'll leave out balances and purchases.
